method.arbitrage: swap toward the venue USD price from outside the band -ln(1 - fee); one event per block and side
method.sigma: venue realized volatility per hour from 5 s returns (Binance ETHUSDT 1 s x Coinbase USDT-USD)
method.band: Fables' resolved fee per second (FeePoked, PoolConfigured), time-averaged per hour
method.model: events/s = 1 / (dt (eta + c)), eta = gamma / (sigma sqrt(dt/2)); c = 1 Poisson, 0.824 fixed
method.hoursKept: hours with at least 5 events and a rate the model can produce

hourly.scope: all weeks (0 to 4); the chosen dt uses the fit weeks only

delay.note: lower bound: an arbitrage is only seen if the venue is still outside the band when it lands, and timestamps are whole seconds

chosen.rule: median hourly frequency inversion, Poisson (c = 1), fit weeks only

sensitivity.zShiftNote: reference price moved by the given bp before classifying arbitrages (z +- 1e-4); same hours, sigma and band
sensitivity.eventPerSecondSideNote: one event per (second, side) instead of per (block, side)

caveats: the per-hour estimate is very sensitive to the band: a 1 bp shift in the reference price, either way, changes the late weeks several-fold (sensitivity.zShiftBp)
the rate model did not hold out: the fit-week dt over-predicts the test weeks' arbitrage counts (holdout)
Jensen effect: the band enters the non-linear rate model as an hourly time average, so an hour mixing floor and storm fees is not equivalent to its average band
the delay method is a lower bound (whole-second timestamps, arbitrages seen only if the venue is still outside the band)
framing: dt_eff is of order 1 to 3 s; the per-hour estimate is very sensitive to the band (a 1 bp shift in the reference price moves weeks 4-5 from ~13 s to ~3-4.5 s). clim's posted fee does not depend on dt: eta is calibrated at equal average fee, so only eta*sqrt(dt/2) matters.
